headline: Held public hearing on borrowing additional $345,000 for Four Hills Landfill PFAS pilot project; no vote recorded on the resolution.
summary: The Board held a public hearing on Resolution R-26-057, which would approve borrowing an additional $345,000 from the Clean Water State Revolving Fund for the Four Hills Landfill PFAS/leachate removal and destruction pilot test project. No one spoke for or against it, and the hearing was closed. The minutes do not record a vote on the resolution before the meeting was adjourned.
plain_text:
A special meeting of the Board of Aldermen was held Monday, September 28, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. in the aldermanic 
chamber and duly noticed in two places, including the City’s website, in accordance with the requirements of RSA 91-
A:2 II. 
 
President Lori Wilshire presided; Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr., recorded. 
 
Prayer was offered by Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr.; Alderman Derek Thibeault led in the Pledge to the 
Flag. 
 
Let’s start the meeting by taking a roll call attendance.   
 
Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr., called the roll. 
 
The roll call was taken with 11 members of the Board of Aldermen present:  Alderman Klee, Alderman Ravan, 
Alderman Thibeault, Alderman O’Brien, Alderman Gregg, Alderman Dowd, Alderman Sullivan, Alderman Sennott  (via 
Zoom), Alderman Johnson, Alderwoman Kelly, President Wilshire.       
 
Alderman Clemons, Alderwoman Smith, Alderman Morgan, and Alderman Lopez were recorded absent. 
 
President Wilshire turned the meeting over to Chairman Dowd. 
 
PUBLIC HEARING 
 
R-26-057 
APPROVING THE BORROWING OF AN ADDITIONAL THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-FIVE THOUSAND 
DOLLARS ($345,000) FROM THE CLEAN WATER STATE REVOLVING FUND FOR THE FOUR HILLS LANDFILL 
PFAS / LEACHATE REMOVAL AND DESTRUCTION PILOT TEST PROJECT 
 
Jeff Lafleur, Superintendent of Solid Waste 
 
So last year as you recall, I went to – I came forward to you people to approve $850,000 or so dollars from the State 
to do a PFAS Pilot Program.  We got those proceeds, we went out to bid, we got a vendor and everything, and we 
found out that it was going to be a little bit more money so we approached the State and they agreed to give us the 
rest of the funding to finish off the project.  So this is that added monies that are needed to continue the process.  
 
Chairman Dowd 
 
Okay.  Any amplifying questions from anyone?  Thank you Jeff. 
 
Now I’ll open up for testimony in favor. 
 
Testimony in Favor - None 
 
Testimony in Opposition - None 
 
Testimony in Favor - None 
 
Testimony in Opposition - None 
 
Chairman Dowd closed the public hearing on Resolution R-26-057 at 7:04 p.m. 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
 
MOTION BY ALDERMAN O’BRIEN THAT THE SEPTEMBER 28, 2026 SPECIAL MEETING OF THE BOARD OF 
ALDERMEN BE ADJOURNED, BY ROLL CALL 
 
A viva voce roll call was taken, which resulted as follows: 
 
Yea: Alderman Klee, Alderman Ravan, Alderwoman Smith,  Alderman Thibeault,  
 Alderman O’Brien, Alderman Gregg, Alderman Dowd, Alderman Sullivan,  
 Alderman Sennott, Alderman Johnson, Alderwoman Kelly, Alderman Wilshire   11
Special Board of Aldermen                                          09-28-2026                        Page 2 
 
 
Nay:                       0 
 
MOTION CARRIED 
 
The meeting was declared adjourned at 7:05 p.m.   
 
                Alderman-at-Large Michael B. O’Brien, Sr. 
                Clerk
